A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a fibrolameller carcinoma can evolve into an adult-type carcinoma, and vice versa.

the fibrolamella hepatocellular carcinoma is a more aggressive tumor with an increased tendency of malignant transformation, and that the central adult-type hepatocarcinoma in our case was probably derived from a malignant transformation of the peripheral tumor.
a fibrolameller-type hepatocellular cancer is not a separate entity but a variant of an adult-type hepatocelluar carcinoma.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of a peripheral mass encasing a central ovoid mass in a hepatic tumor of a young patient should raise the suspicion of fibrolamellar carcinoma.

the presence of a central tumor mass in a fibrolamellated hepatocellular carcinoma should raise the suspicion of the presence of a concomitant adult-type hepatocarcinoma, even if the latter may be small and clinically silent.
the 2 variants may share a common etiologic pathway.
